question.leadin: This woman was the last ruler of the Ptolemaic [tall-uh-may-ik] dynasty.
question.text: Name this last queen of independent Egypt before it was conquered by the Romans.
question.clue: This ruler allegedly won a bet by drinking pearls dissolved in vinegar, and while besieged by enemies, this monarch asked for and received a basket of figs.

swap.leadin: This son of Akhenaten ruled with the assistance of the vizier Ay ("eye"), who eventually succeeded him after his death.
swap.text: Name this "Boy Pharaoh" of Egypt, whose tomb was famously discovered nearly intact by Howard Carter.
swap.clue: One of this ruler's names which invoked the god Aten was changed after his "Restoration" reversed his probable father's monotheism.

question.text: The only remaining wonder of the ancient world is this structure, which was built for Pharaoh Khufu [koo-foo] at Giza.
question.answerHtml: The Great Pyramid of Giza (accept The Great Pyramid of Khufu or reasonable equivalents)
question.clue: Slave labor was long thought to have been used to build this structure, but many archaeologists believe that thousands of skilled laborers were used instead over a 20 year period.

swap.text: King Tut's tomb was discovered by this man who lost many comrades, including expedition leader Lord Carnarvon, after an alleged "mummy's curse".
swap.clue: Starting at age 17, this person worked for Gaston Maspero, who provided a recommendation for a later employer.

question.leadin: This battle was fought along the Orontes River.
question.text: Name this battle fought between forces divided into divisions such as Ra and Amun against Hittite forces under Muwatalli II.
question.clue: Hugo Winckler discovered records of this battle after excavating one side's capital of Hattusa.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about ancient treaties.
swap.text: The earliest known peace treaty was signed after the Battle of Kadesh by the Hittites under Hattusili III and the Egyptians under this pharaoh whose other accomplishments include the construction of Abu Simbel.
swap.clue: This son of Seti completed the hypostyle hall at Karnak, commissioned a giant statue of himself at Abu Simbel, and signed the world's first peace treaty with the Hittites following a huge chariot battle at Kadesh.

question.leadin: George Cecil Ives founded an "Order" named for this city's greatest defeat, which is commemorated by a statue of a lion.
question.text: Name this city state that employed an elite military unit of 300 homosexual lovers known as its "Sacred Band."
question.clue: Troops from this city employed the "cutting off the snake's head" technique to defeat Cleombrotus of Sparta.

swap.leadin: The Sherden pirates may have been one tribe of these people.
swap.text: Name this loose group who frequently attacked ancient Egypt during the collapse of the Bronze Age.
swap.clue: A confederation of them known as the Nine Bows was fought by Merneptah, and they were responsible for the fall of Ugarit.

question.leadin: This region's Queen Ati was depicted in an ancient relief at the Deir el-Bahri (DAYR el-BAHR-i) complex.
question.text: Name this region from which a 16th-century B.C. Egyptian expedition brought back frankincense and live myrrh trees.
question.clue: An expedition to this place led by the Chancellor Nehsi was recorded in inscriptions in the mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahri.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Ancient Egyptian agriculture.
swap.text: Irrigation canals were dug in order to control and store the water generated from this annual event. Egyptians would plant their crops in October after the end of this event.
swap.answerHtml: flooding of the Nile [or obvious equivalents indicating the overflow or inundation of the Nile River; prompt on floods]

question.leadin: The word aamu may refer to these people during their early contacts.
question.text: Name these people who invaded Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period. These people, who introduced the chariot to Egypt, constituted Egypt's Fifteenth Dynasty.
question.clue: Their capital was at Avaris, and they were overthrown by Ahmose.

swap.leadin: Name the following associated with 's 18th dynasty.
swap.text: Husband of Nefertiti, he is known for rejecting the standard pantheon of Egyptian gods and erecting a large temple to an Egyptian sun-god.
swap.clue: Like his father, who married a non-royal woman named Tiy, he married a woman who was not of royal blood, the daughter of a vizier named Ay.

question.text: The existence of this pharaoh is attested to by a namesake palette that depicts him with two crowns. This pharaoh was the unifier of Upper and Lower Egypt.
question.clue: This pharaoh who unified Upper and Lower Egypt and is depicted on a namesake palette wearing the crowns of both parts. Alternatively, name the legendary unifier of Egypt who is often identified with him.

swap.leadin: Emperor Claudius wrote a letter to the inhabitants of a city in this province about Jewish freedom of worship.
swap.text: Name this region that became a Roman province a decade after its Queen Arsinoe was executed in Rome.
swap.clue: By the 1st century C.E. this province produced the largest share of the cura annonae.

question.leadin: This king described his extensive repairs of buildings destroyed in a storm in the Tempest Stele.
question.text: Identify this son of Seqenenre Tao, the first pharaoh of the Egyptian 18th dynasty. This king rebuilt the much-weakened civil service in Thebes, which he re-established as the capital of Egypt.
question.answerHtml: Ahmose I [or Amosis I; or Neb-Pehty-Re; prompt on partial answer]
question.clue: The 18th Dynasty was founded by this monarch, who successfully expelled the Hyksos from the country. He also reestablished Egyptian control over Nubia.

swap.text: This Egyptian god was usually depicted as a pharaoh except for his unusual feather-decorated crown and his green skin.

question.text: The pyramid at el-Lahun, or Kahun, was designed for the second pharaoh of this name, who also built a great dike there. Except for its last female ruler Sobekneferu, the entire Twelfth Dynasty consisted only of pharaohs with this name or Amenemhat.
question.clue: This name of three Twelfth Dynasty pharaohs. Herodotus gave this name's Greek equivalent to a pharaoh who supposedly erected genitalia-topped columns to mock the cities he conquered in Asia Minor and Thrace.

swap.leadin: This city was a cult center for the ram god Heryshaf.
swap.text: Name this Ancient Egyptian city south of the Fayum that dominated Lower Egypt during the First Intermediate Period, in opposition to Thebes in the north. Mentuhotep II (men-TOO-hoh-tep "the second") conquered this city to reunify Egypt into the Middle Kingdom.

question.text: Though most Egyptologists agree that ancient Egyptians were not black, they are certain that pharaohs from this dynasty were black. This last dynasty in the Third Intermediate Period lasted from 760 BC to 656 BC, and its fall marked the beginning of the Late Period.

swap.leadin: An expedition here was reportedly made by the Fifth Dynasty pharaoh Sahure, while later trips were made by Mentuhotep III and finally Ramses III. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this kingdom allegedly in existence from 2500-1170 in Eastern Africa. It's frequently cited as a source of myrrh, ebony, rare wood, and exotic animals like giraffes - as attested by scenes on the temple of Hatshepsut.
swap.clue: A state named in honor of this place was led in the early 20th century by the Warsangali Sultanate and was centered at Garowe.
